The question asks for every game in the data, so I used `RAW.raw_games_details` directly rather than a view that might filter by season or game type. The grain is one row per game, team and player, so I removed duplicate source rows first. I then summed points per player and took the top 5. I didn't run the query.

```sql
WITH dedup AS (
  SELECT GAME_ID, TEAM_ID, PLAYER_ID, PLAYER_NAME, PTS
  FROM RAW.raw_games_details
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY GAME_ID, TEAM_ID, PLAYER_ID
    ORDER BY PTS DESC NULLS LAST, MIN DESC NULLS LAST
  ) = 1
)
SELECT
  PLAYER_ID,
  ANY_VALUE(PLAYER_NAME) AS player_name,
  SUM(PTS) AS total_points
FROM dedup
WHERE PTS IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY PLAYER_ID
ORDER BY total_points DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

The query uses `TRANSFORMED.local_player_game_facts`, which has one deduplicated row per player per game and no filter on game type, so preseason and playoff games are included. A double-double is a game with at least two of points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks at 10 or more. I filter to season 2017 and to games the player actually played, then count those games per player and take the top one. I haven't run it. Ties are broken by player name.

```sql
SELECT
  player_id,
  player_name,
  COUNT(*) AS double_doubles
FROM TRANSFORMED.local_player_game_facts
WHERE season = 2017
  AND participated
  AND (
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(points, 0) >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(rebounds, 0) >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(assists, 0) >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(steals, 0) >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(blocks, 0) >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
  ) >= 2
GROUP BY player_id, player_name
ORDER BY double_doubles DESC, player_name
LIMIT 1;
```

The query uses `RAW.raw_games`, which holds every game, rather than the canonicalized team-game table. It looks up the Nets' team ID from `raw_teams` by city and nickname. A game counts as a Nets win if they were the home team and `HOME_TEAM_WINS = 1`, or the visitor and `HOME_TEAM_WINS = 0`. I count distinct `GAME_ID`s in case the raw table has duplicate rows. I haven't run it against the data.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT g.GAME_ID) AS nets_wins_2020
FROM RAW.raw_games g
JOIN RAW.raw_teams t
  ON t.CITY = 'Brooklyn' AND t.NICKNAME = 'Nets'
WHERE g.SEASON = 2020
  AND (
    (g.HOME_TEAM_ID = t.TEAM_ID AND g.HOME_TEAM_WINS = 1)
    OR (g.VISITOR_TEAM_ID = t.TEAM_ID AND g.HOME_TEAM_WINS = 0)
  );
```

The query filters `RAW.raw_games` to `SEASON = 2018` with no game-status filter, so preseason and playoff games are all counted. It deduplicates by game, computes each home team's win rate as the average of `HOME_TEAM_WINS`, and joins `RAW.raw_teams` for the abbreviation. I haven't run it against the data.

```sql
WITH g AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT GAME_ID, HOME_TEAM_ID, HOME_TEAM_WINS
  FROM RAW.raw_games
  WHERE SEASON = 2018
)
SELECT t.ABBREVIATION AS team_abbreviation,
       ROUND(AVG(g.HOME_TEAM_WINS::DOUBLE), 3) AS home_win_rate
FROM g
JOIN RAW.raw_teams t ON t.TEAM_ID = g.HOME_TEAM_ID
GROUP BY t.ABBREVIATION, g.HOME_TEAM_ID
ORDER BY AVG(g.HOME_TEAM_WINS::DOUBLE) DESC, t.ABBREVIATION
LIMIT 1;
```

This query uses `RAW.raw_games` for every game in season 2016, so preseason and playoff games are included. It de-duplicates by game, since the repo's own "canonical game" wording hints at duplicate source rows. It then credits each game to both teams, with the home margin to the home team and the negative of it to the visitor. Summing per team gives the differential, and `RAW.raw_teams` supplies the abbreviation. I haven't run it against the data.

```sql
WITH g AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT GAME_ID, HOME_TEAM_ID, VISITOR_TEAM_ID, PTS_home, PTS_away
  FROM RAW.raw_games
  WHERE SEASON = 2016
    AND PTS_home IS NOT NULL
    AND PTS_away IS NOT NULL
),
t AS (
  SELECT HOME_TEAM_ID AS team_id, PTS_home - PTS_away AS diff FROM g
  UNION ALL
  SELECT VISITOR_TEAM_ID AS team_id, PTS_away - PTS_home AS diff FROM g
)
SELECT tm.ABBREVIATION AS team_abbreviation,
       SUM(t.diff) AS point_differential
FROM t
JOIN RAW.raw_teams tm ON tm.TEAM_ID = t.team_id
GROUP BY tm.ABBREVIATION
ORDER BY point_differential DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

This counts each game once, credits the win to the home team when `HOME_TEAM_WINS = 1` and to the visitor otherwise, then joins to `RAW.raw_teams` for the abbreviation. It filters on `SEASON = 2017` with no game-type filter, so preseason and playoff games are included. I haven't run it against the data. If several teams tie for the top spot, it returns only one of them.

```sql
WITH g AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT GAME_ID, HOME_TEAM_ID, VISITOR_TEAM_ID, HOME_TEAM_WINS
  FROM RAW.raw_games
  WHERE SEASON = 2017
    AND HOME_TEAM_WINS IS NOT NULL
),
w AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN HOME_TEAM_WINS = 1 THEN HOME_TEAM_ID ELSE VISITOR_TEAM_ID END AS winner_id
  FROM g
)
SELECT t.ABBREVIATION AS team_abbreviation, COUNT(*) AS wins
FROM w
JOIN RAW.raw_teams t ON t.TEAM_ID = w.winner_id
GROUP BY t.ABBREVIATION
ORDER BY wins DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

Approach: I'm using `TRANSFORMED.local_player_game_facts`, which has one deduplicated row per player per game across the full history, so preseason and playoff games are included. A double-double is a game with at least two of points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks at 10 or more. I group by player ID rather than name so two players sharing a name aren't merged. I haven't run the query against the data.

```sql
SELECT
  player_id,
  MAX(player_name) AS player_name,
  COUNT(*) AS double_doubles
FROM TRANSFORMED.local_player_game_facts
WHERE (
  (COALESCE(points, 0) >= 10)::INT +
  (COALESCE(rebounds, 0) >= 10)::INT +
  (COALESCE(assists, 0) >= 10)::INT +
  (COALESCE(steals, 0) >= 10)::INT +
```

Games are hosted at the home team's arena, so I join each 2019-season game to its home team's arena and count the games per arena. The arena with the highest count is the answer.

```sql
SELECT t.ARENA, COUNT(DISTINCT g.GAME_ID) AS games_hosted
FROM RAW.raw_games g
JOIN RAW.raw_teams t ON g.HOME_TEAM_ID = t.TEAM_ID
WHERE g.SEASON = 2019
GROUP BY t.ARENA
ORDER BY games_hosted DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

Approach: take each game once from `RAW.raw_games` for season 2018 (deduplicated by `GAME_ID`) and credit the win to the home or visitor team. Then count wins per team, take the top team, and join to `RAW.raw_teams` for its head coach. Because there is no filter on game type, preseason and playoff games are all counted.

```sql
WITH g AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT GAME_ID, HOME_TEAM_ID, VISITOR_TEAM_ID, HOME_TEAM_WINS
  FROM RAW.raw_games
  WHERE SEASON = 2018
),
wins AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN HOME_TEAM_WINS = 1 THEN HOME_TEAM_ID ELSE VISITOR_TEAM_ID END AS team_id,
         COUNT(*) AS w
  FROM g
  WHERE HOME_TEAM_WINS IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT t.HEADCOACH
FROM wins
JOIN RAW.raw_teams t ON t.TEAM_ID = wins.team_id
ORDER BY wins.w DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
